_comment: Prediction-engine weights, tuned per tour x surface by walk-forward log loss (data-pipeline/tuneWeights.js). Each match's SMASH probability = calibrate(ws*simProb + we*eloProb + wr*rankProb). rankProb(p1) = 1/(1+10^((log10(rankA)-log10(rankB))*rankScale)).
_calibrationComment: One-parameter Platt recalibration applied to the SMASH blend only: p' = sigmoid(a * logit(p)). The intercept is pinned at 0 by symmetry (which side is p1 is arbitrary), so a pick can never flip, only its stated confidence moves. a is refit per tour by tuneWeights.js on walk-forward out-of-fold predictions at every retune; a < 1 compresses overconfident tails. Replaced the hand-fit knee/factor tail shrink (validated equal-or-better in data-pipeline/experiments.js).
_eloComment: Elo hyperparameters. rho = weight on overall vs surface rating in the predicting blend; marginK scales rating updates by set dominance (straight-sets wins move ratings more than deciding-set escapes); kScale/kExp are the K-factor schedule, K = kScale/(n+5)^kExp. marginK and the schedule are set PER TOUR (blocks below override the shared root values); rho is NOT, because src/engines.js also reads it in the browser, so a per-tour rho would desync the live prediction from the graded record. Validated on the FULL raw match cache (~30k matches per tour, 2015-2026) by data-pipeline/backtestBayes.js via .github/workflows/verify-ratings.yml, sweeping on the earlier half of the graded season and scoring on the later half. ATP holdout 0.6497 -> 0.6373 log loss and 62.2% -> 63.7% accuracy for the current block; WTA keeps 150/0, which no config in a 240-point sweep beat on both metrics, at 0.6303 and 64.7%. The figures this comment carried before (ATP 68.2 -> 73.8%, WTA 69.5 -> 74.7%) were measured before the match-identity dedupe and are withdrawn: roughly two in five rows in both the training timeline and the holdout were repeats of the same fixture, which inflated the apparent gain and, on the ATP, pointed at the wrong schedule entirely.
_scorelineComment: Set-probability temperature for the exact-score distribution ONLY (win probabilities untouched). Real sets are positively correlated - favorites sweep more often than independent-sets math implies - so best-of-five scorelines sharpen the set prob before the negative binomial. Fitted walk-forward (experiments.js scoreline): bo5 exact-score accuracy 24.4% -> 30.4%; best-of-three is structurally insensitive (modal is 2-0 whenever the favorite clears 0.5) and stays untempered.
